messages.body_plain:
Hello Walt,

there is certainly several ways of doing this, here is the one I would use.

> ttt <- matrix(c(0, 0, NA, 0, 0, NA, rep (0, 4), NA, 0), nrow = 3, byrow =
T)
> row.names(ttt) <- c("TL", "JAR", "TM")
> colnames(ttt) <- c(LETTERS[1:4])
> ttt
    A  B  C D
 TL 0  0 NA 0
JAR 0 NA  0 0
 TM 0  0 NA 0
> which.na(ttt) ## Returns the indices of the NA's in column major format.
[1] 5 7 9

## You may, or may not, know that Splus internally represents matrices in a
long vector, stored column by
## column.  A few years ago I wrote a little function to the convert an
index of a Column Major
## representation of a matrix to the more familiar row, column indices.

> ColumnMajor(index = which.na(ttt), dimension = dim(ttt))
     row col
[1,]   2   2
[2,]   1   3
[3,]   3   3
>

>From here on you only need to index the row names and column names of your
matrix.

Here is the litte "ColumnMajor" function.

"ColumnMajor" <- function(index, dimension)
{
### Author : Gérald Jean
### Date   :  2 Oct 2003, 10:36
### Purpose: will return the row and column index of a matrix of dimension
###          "dimension" for the index "index" of a Column Major
represention
###          of the matrix.
### ----------------------------------------------------------------------
### Arguments:
###  index    : the index in the vector representing the matrix in Column
Major
###             representation.
###  dimension: the dimension of the matrix.
### ----------------------------------------------------------------------

  m       <- dimension[1]
  modulo  <- index %% m
  int.div <- index %/% m
  row.ind <- ifelse(modulo == 0, m, modulo)
  col.ind <- ifelse(modulo == 0, int.div, int.div + 1)
  cbind(row = row.ind, col = col.ind)
}

messages.subject: Re: Load Linux workspace in Windows
messages.body_plain:
On Sun, Oct 10, 2010 at 11:23:02PM +0300, Adal Chiriliuc wrote:

> Is it possible to load an S-PLUS Linux workspace in Windows?
> 
> If I try it I get this error: "Problem in exists(name, where = db):
> This directory has both Unix style ___nonfile and Windows style
> ___nonfi"
> 
> The __nonfi file is created when I first try to load that Linux
> workspace in Windows.
> 
> Is there any way to convert it to a Windows workspace?

Yes. The easiest approach is to recreate the workspace in Linux such
that it is compatible with Windows.

To do this, in Linux, start S-PLUS and then use data.dump() to write out
all the objects in the workspace:

    data.dump(objects(), "allObjects.sdd")

Then create a new workspace that can be used with both Linux and
Windows. At the Linux shell do:

    mv .Data .Data.orig
    Splus CHAPTER -type Windows  # Creates a new .Data

Now restart S-PLUS and restore the objects in allObjects.sdd:

    data.retore("allObjects.sdd")

The new workspace will have all the objects from the original one and be
accessible from both Linux and Windows. Be aware that if you have
hundreds or thousands of objects or some very large objects, the above
data.dump() and data.restore() may take several minutes.

Background details: S-PLUS uses the operating system's file system to
store objects. The Windows file system is more restrictive that Linux
e.g. you cannot have files called xyzzy and XYZZY in the same directory
but those are two different object names in S-PLUS. When the file name
cannot match the object name, S-PLUS uses its nonfile mechanize to create
a file in .Data with the name __n where n is some positive integer. The
file ___nonfile (Linux) or ___nonfi (Windows) contains information to
map the __n file name to the S-PLUS object name.  The presence of the
___nonfile file in .Data (instead of ___nonfi) indicates to S-PLUS for
Windows that the objects in this workspace were created under a less
restrictive file system and Windows may not be able to distinguish
the different objects based on file name alone.

-Stephen Kaluzny
 TIBCO Software Inc.

All,
  That sounds like a very appealing way to compute age, but timeSpan does 
not know about leap years. Take this as an example:
> timeDate('03/01/2000') - timeDate('03/01/1964') -> DT
> DT@format <- "%y years + %D days"
> DT
[1] 36 years + 9 days
   This would clearly result in reporting the wrong age in some cases. 
Note that Walt would be 61 on 10/20/2010!
  I do not have a function for computing age, but the age can be computed 
by using mdy to compute the month day and year of each date. Then compute 
the differences, call them yd, md, and dd.
If md is > 0, then the age is yd,
else if md == 0 and dd > 0, then age is yd,
otherwise age is yd - 1
Dave

The S+ package system uses Rd files as the source format for help files.
When the package is installed under Unix/Linux the Rd files are
converted (magically) to html. On Windows the Rd files are all converted
into a Windows CHM file.

If you submit your package to CSAN (the S+ package repository), a binary

source version. To submit a package to CSAN, send the source archive
(.zip or .tar.gz) via email to: s-packages at tibco.com

messages.subject: Re: Generate samples from Empirical pdf
messages.body_plain:
To sample from the empirical distribution, use 
  sample(x, size = length(x), replace = TRUE)

To sample from a kernel density estimate, use
  sample(x, size = length(x), replace = TRUE) + rnorm(length(x)) * sd
where sd is the desired standard deviation of the kernel.
The smoothed bootstrap in the resample library uses 
  stdev(x)/sqrt(length(x)),
as this makes the expected variance of the smoothed distribution equal
to sigma^2; see
Hesterberg, Tim C. (2004), Unbiasing the Bootstrap-Bootknife Sampling vs. Smoothing, Proceedings of the Section on Statistics and the Environment, American Statistical Association, 2924-2930.
http://home.comcast.net/~timhesterberg/articles/JSM04-bootknife.pdf

messages.body_plain:
Hello Peter,
One way to work around this is to rename the 
first Access database after you have exported the 
first dataframe. Call this Family.mdb. Then go 
back to S-Plus and export the second dataframe to 
its own Access database, say Test.mdb.  Then open 
the first Access database (Family.mdb) and use 
the File > get to import the second table from Test.mdb into Family.mdb.

Repeat as needed.

BTW, I use the S-Plus menu File > Import rather than the command.

Best wishes,
